root_cause.text: The mm/memfd_luo preserve path serialized each folio’s dirty state at preserve time even though a mapped folio can become dirty later and its PTE dirty bit may not yet be synced, causing restored memfd folios with user data to be incorrectly marked clean and reclaimable.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and added comment state that “memfd preservation with LUO saves the flag at preserve(). This is problematic. The folio might get dirtied later,” that saving at freeze also fails because “the dirty bit from PTE is normally synced at unmap,” and the patch fixes this by calling `folio_mark_dirty(folio);` and always setting `pfolio->flags = MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY | MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_UPTODATE;`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused local variable from `memfd_luo_preserve_folios()` to simplify the loop without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration `unsigned int flags = 0;` was removed from inside the `for` loop in `memfd_luo_preserve_folios()`, with no other code changes shown in the hunk.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior because the removed variable was unused in the shown code; it only eliminates an unnecessary local declaration from each loop iteration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always mark preserved folios dirty to prevent reclaimed clean-state restoration from losing user data after live update.
intent_record.what: The code removes the conditional check `if (folio_test_dirty(folio)) flags |= MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY;` and replaces it with an unconditional call to `folio_mark_dirty(folio);`, along with a detailed comment explaining why the dirty state is now forced during folio preservation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, every preserved folio is now explicitly marked dirty instead of only recording whether it was dirty at that moment. This prevents folios that become dirty after preservation from later being treated as clean and reclaimable after retrieval, avoiding possible loss of user data, at the cost of keeping originally clean folios non-reclaimable after live update.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always save preserved folios with both DIRTY and UPTODATE flags to ensure correct folio state metadata.
intent_record.what: The code removes the statement that ORed MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_UPTODATE into the local flags variable, and instead changes the assignment to pfolio->flags so it always stores MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY | MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_UPTODATE directly rather than the computed flags value.
intent_record.how: At runtime, preserved folios are now always recorded with both DIRTY and UPTODATE bits set in pfolio->flags, regardless of the prior contents of the local flags variable. This prevents the saved folio metadata from omitting the DIRTY bit or depending on earlier flag accumulation logic.

Always save preserved folios with both DIRTY and UPTODATE flags to ensure correct folio state metadata.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure preserved folios are always saved with the correct state metadata, including DIRTY and UPTODATE flags, to prevent data loss or incorrect restoration after live update.

relevance_review.reason: The change only removes an unused local variable and explicitly does not alter behavior in memfd_luo_preserve_folios(); it does not address dirty-state serialization, PTE dirty-bit syncing, or folios being incorrectly restored as clean.

The vulnerability is caused by preserved memfd folios being serialized with an incorrect clean state, allowing restored folios containing user data to be reclaimable. This group directly fixes that by always preserving folios with DIRTY (and UPTODATE) state metadata, matching the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This conditional serialized the folio DIRTY state only at preserve time. A mapped folio could become dirty later via a PTE dirty bit not yet synced to the folio, so relying on this test caused preserved folios with user data to be restored as clean.

This statement is part of the flawed conditional dirty-state recording logic. Because it executed only when folio_test_dirty() was true at preserve time, folios with later-unsynced dirtying were saved without the DIRTY flag and could be reclaimed incorrectly.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional is the root of the bug: it records the folio dirty state only at preserve time. A mapped folio may become dirty later through an unsynced PTE dirty bit, so gating preservation of the dirty flag on this check allows folios containing user data to be restored as clean and reclaimable.

This statement participates in the vulnerable logic because it executes only under the preserve-time folio_test_dirty() condition. As a result, folios dirtied later via unsynced PTE state are preserved without the dirty flag, enabling incorrect clean restoration and possible data loss on reclaim.

mm: memfd_luo: allow preserving memfd

The ability to preserve a memfd allows userspace to use KHO and LUO to

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit b3749f174d686627f702234e64bad976dc432dbc
Author: Pratyush Yadav <pratyush@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Nov 25 11:58:44 2025 -0500

    mm: memfd_luo: allow preserving memfd
    
    The ability to preserve a memfd allows userspace to use KHO and LUO to
    transfer its memory contents to the next kernel.  This is useful in many
    ways.  For one, it can be used with IOMMUFD as the backing store for IOMMU
    page tables.  Preserving IOMMUFD is essential for performing a hypervisor
    live up
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains both the preserve-side serialization of folio state and the restore-side use of that serialized state. In `memfd_luo_preserve_folios()`, each folio's dirty state is snapshotted at preserve time: `if (folio_test_dirty(folio)) flags |= MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY;` and then stored into `pfolio->flags = flags;`. The file is only frozen around preserve/unpreserve (`shmem_freeze(inode, true);` in `memfd_luo_preserve()` and later `shmem_freeze(inode, false);`), and the commit message states the file can still be written after preserve; there is no later resynchronization of dirty state in `memfd_luo_freeze()`, which only updates `ser->pos`. On restore, `memfd_luo_retrieve_folios()` re-applies the serialized dirty bit with `if (flags & MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY) folio_mark_dirty(folio);`. Therefore, if a mapped folio becomes dirty after preserve time and before handover, that later dirtiness is not captured, and the restored folio can be incorrectly left clean. The fix would require avoiding this stale per-folio dirty snapshot or re-evaluating/syncing dirty state at the final handoff point; no such handling is present here.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows both the preserve-side serialization of folio state and the restore-side reapplication of that state. In `memfd_luo_preserve_folios()`, the code snapshots dirty state once during preserve: `if (folio_test_dirty(folio)) flags |= MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY;` and stores it in `pfolio->flags = flags;`. Later, in `memfd_luo_retrieve_folios()`, that serialized bit is used to restore the folio state: `if (flags & MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY) folio_mark_dirty(folio);`. This matches the root cause exactly: dirty state is serialized at preserve time per folio, even though a mapped folio may become dirty later and page-table dirty state may not yet be synced into the folio flag. The commit message itself says, `The file can still be read from or written to` after preservation, and `memfd_luo_preserve()` freezes the inode only during preserve via `shmem_freeze(inode, true);`, while `memfd_luo_freeze()` later updates only `ser->pos` with the comment `The pos might have changed since prepare. Everything else stays the same.` There is no logic in the freeze/finalization path to rescan folio dirty state, sync PTE dirty bits, or conservatively mark restored folios dirty. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present.
